codeManifestHash.description: Content identity of the revision's code paths only (C2). Stamped beside manifestHash so a code-scoped verdict can outlive a governance-text edit; absent when the split cannot be derived, in which case a code-scoped binding refuses to match.

governanceManifestHash.description: The governance-text surface at the time of this verdict (§22/§24). A text-only edit expires what this surface was verified for, and nothing else.

instrumentManifestHash.description: The declared-instrument surface at the time of this verdict (§24.4). Editing a declared instrument expires the instrument surface only — not the pass about the deliverable.

candidateFreezeSha256.description: The frozen candidate this verdict answered (§7.4). Stamped beside the manifest so the conclusion binds to the reviewed content and semantic contract rather than to the declared owned paths, which cannot see a change committed outside the declaration.

reviewedRevisionId.description: The revision this round actually reviewed, when that is not the revision it is recorded against. The binding fields describe the content the record is bound to; this names the revision the round was opened against, so a round recorded after the content moved can be told apart from one that answered the content in hand. Absent on records written before the field existed, which is history that cannot claim either.

subjectRevision.description: The ledger subject this round answered — the claim set and plan the request was built from. Recorded so a later round can tell whether a recorded result answered *this* request or an earlier one; a record without it (written before this field existed) keeps blocking, because we cannot know what it answered.

reviewedPaths.description: The owned paths this review actually read (design §F5). Optional; when absent the review is treated as covering the whole revision, which is the conservative reading.

assurance.description: The read vocabulary, so a historical review stays readable (see READABLE_ASSURANCE_LEVELS). The retired values (sandboxed, signed) are refused on the write side by the approval guard and by `ledger decide --assurance`, because a schema cannot express 'readable here, unwritable there' in one enum.

declaredCoverage.description: The claim ids the round declared it read and found sound. Written with an empty findings list, because an empty result and a result that read nothing are different facts and only this field tells them apart.

findingsWithoutClass.description: The findings in this record that carry no defect class. Reported rather than refused: a payload written before the field existed must still record, and the gap has to be a measured fact instead of a silent hole.

triggerClasses.description: The recurring defect classes the round was asked to explain, named as the packet named them.

conclusion.description: The single root cause the round concluded, from a closed vocabulary so a later reader can compare two rounds rather than two essays.

evidence.description: The concrete records and source references that separate this conclusion from the alternatives it was asked to rule out.

nextAction.description: What the conclusion permits next. Paired with the conclusion by the validator, because a root cause that asks for the wrong next step is how a loop keeps buying rounds: behaviour_defect, instrument_unsound and workflow_routing_error require repair, claim_scope_error requires restate_claim, not_same_class requires resume_certification.

recurrenceAnalysis.description: The durable root-cause conclusion of a round that was dispatched as a recurrence round (`recurrencePacket` present on the request). Recorded because the whole point of the packet is that the next reader can see what the previous round concluded — a conclusion that lives only in a transcript is the finding that vanishes (I-22) one layer up.
